summary: HR calendar (company-wide, built for hundreds of people)
description: The dashboard calendar draws one bar per person per request, which is unreadable at the BRD's ~800 staff. HR Admin gets a separate page that shows how many people are out each day, filterable by team (manager) and leave type, and a day opens the list of who is out. Read-only, HR Admin only; managers keep the existing team calendar on the dashboard. Additive: no role change, no existing page changes. Not in the PRD (docs rule: no PRD edit); the acceptance criteria live in these rows.

summary: HR calendar read: daily counts and a day's list, filtered and bounded
description: Two reads in src/lib/leave/, each ONE statement, hr_admin only. (1) For a month: per day, the number of people out (approved always; pending as a separate count) by leave type, with optional filters manager_id and leave_type_id; generate_series over the month joined to non-deleted requests that overlap it, weekdays only, never scanning past the month. (2) For one day: the people out that day (name, team manager, leave type, dates, status), paged 25 at a time and filterable by name. Rejected and deleted requests excluded. Dates and weekday rules follow calendar.ts and working-days.ts, today in APP_TIMEZONE. Add an index only if EXPLAIN on 800 users and about 8,000 requests shows a need. Tests: exact counts, a request spanning a month boundary, weekends, filters, a real-engine test with a break-the-filter proof.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the month read returns, per weekday, the exact count of people out split by leave type and status, for any team or leave type filter;AC2: a day read lists exactly the people out that day, 25 per page, never deleted or rejected requests;AC3: a request that spans two months is counted in both months and weekends are never counted;AC4: one statement per read and the scope is the hr_admin role plus the filters in the SQL

description: Server page /calendar, requireRole hr_admin (others redirected), a nav item for HR Admin only. Month grid showing, per day, a total and small per-type counts as text (no bar per person), filters for team and leave type kept in the address, previous and next month, today highlighted, a day opens a panel or section listing who is out (TASK-042 day read) with paging and name search. Streamed section with its own failure fallback, skeleton and loading.tsx, empty state, query budget test. Mobile first: a compact month list on phones, nothing horizontal at 375 and 320 px, keyboard-usable, counts and statuses written as text.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR Admin sees the month with the number of people out per day and can filter by team and leave type;AC2: opening a day lists who is out with paging and name search;AC3: a manager or employee cannot open the page;AC4: a failed read says so without breaking the app and an empty month shows an empty state;AC5: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px and nothing is shown by colour alone

summary: HR calendar at scale: load check and validation
description: Generate a throwaway database with 800 users, balances and about 8,000 requests spread over a year (generate_series, scratchpad only, never staging), run the two reads and the page's statements, record the timings and EXPLAIN plans in a retro, and fix a slow query before it ships (the BRD asks for 800 concurrent staff). Browser check at 1440, 375 and 320 px. Full quality gate.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: with 800 users and about 8,000 requests the month read and a day read each finish well inside the page's query deadline (the figures are recorded in the retro);AC2: the quality gate passes;AC3: the browser check passes at 1440, 375 and 320 px
